sections.content: Virginia Beach is more than just a tourist destination. It's a year-round real estate market with a growing population, strong military presence, and consistent rental demand. Whether you're a local investor or exploring from out of state, finding real estate deals in Virginia Beach VA can be a smart move in 2024. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in. This article covers everything you need to know — from market conditions and average prices to the best deal types and neighborhoods worth targeting.
Virginia Beach Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Virginia Beach is the most populous city in Virginia, home to roughly 460,000 residents. It's anchored by Naval Station Norfolk nearby and Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek, which together create a massive, stable base of military renters and buyers. Demand for housing doesn't dry up here the way it might in smaller or less economically diverse cities. The local economy is supported by tourism, healthcare, technology, and the military — a combination that keeps unemployment low and housing demand steady.

As of 2024, the median home price in Virginia Beach sits around $330,000 to $360,000, depending on the neighborhood and property type. That's relatively affordable compared to coastal markets like Miami or Los Angeles, but prices have climbed roughly 18 to 22 percent over the past three years. This appreciation trend creates real upside for investors who buy right. Inventory remains tight in many zip codes, which means motivated sellers and off-market deals carry extra value right now.
In markets driven by a strong military and tourism economy, the fundamentals rarely lie. Consistent population, consistent demand — that's the foundation every real estate investor wants.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Virginia Beach VA

Not every zip code in Virginia Beach offers the same opportunity. Savvy investors focus on areas where distressed inventory exists, rents are rising, or redevelopment is underway. Here are the neighborhoods worth putting on your radar.
Pembroke and Central Virginia Beach

Pembroke is a central district undergoing commercial and residential revitalization. Home prices here range from $270,000 to $340,000, with strong rental demand from young professionals and military families. Older ranch-style homes in this area often make excellent fix-and-flip targets, especially those built in the 1970s and 1980s that haven't been updated.
Kempsville

Kempsville is one of the largest and most established communities in Virginia Beach. It offers a mix of single-family homes and townhouses priced between $260,000 and $380,000. This area attracts stable long-term renters and families, making it ideal for buy-and-hold investors. Gross rental yields here commonly land between 6 and 8 percent on well-priced acquisitions.
Princess Anne and Pungo

If you're looking for land deals, development opportunities, or rural properties with value-add potential, the Princess Anne and Pungo corridors in the southern part of the city are worth exploring. Lots and older farmhouses occasionally hit the market at prices that allow for creative deal structures, including seller financing and subject-to arrangements.
Oceanfront and Resort Area

The Oceanfront strip and surrounding Resort Area cater to short-term rental investors. Condos here range from $200,000 for older units to well over $600,000 for modern builds. Airbnb-friendly zoning and high seasonal demand make this a strong market for vacation rental income, though HOA rules and regulations vary significantly by building.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Virginia Beach
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling in Virginia Beach is active, particularly in older working-class neighborhoods where properties sit vacant or are owned by out-of-state heirs. A typical wholesale deal in this market involves properties priced 20 to 30 percent below ARV (After Repair Value), with assignment fees ranging from $8,000 to $25,000 depending on the deal. If you're new to wholesaling, start with our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide to understand the basics before approaching sellers.
Fix-and-Flip Deals

Fix-and-flip activity is strong in Virginia Beach, especially on properties built between 1960 and 1990 that need cosmetic or moderate rehab work. Average flip margins in the market run between $40,000 and $80,000 before holding costs and financing, depending on scope of work and location. To avoid overpaying, always run your numbers through our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) before making an offer. Knowing your after-repair value before you buy is non-negotiable.
Long-Term Rentals

The military-driven rental market in Virginia Beach is a major advantage for buy-and-hold investors. Active duty service members receive Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH), which means they can afford market-rate rents even during economic downturns. Average rents for a 3-bedroom single-family home range from $1,900 to $2,500 per month depending on location and condition. With median purchase prices around $330,000, cash-on-cash returns of 6 to 9 percent are achievable with the right financing structure.

Pro Tip: Military tenants with BAH often make exceptionally reliable renters. Focus your long-term rental acquisitions within a 15-minute commute of Naval Station Norfolk or Little Creek to tap into this tenant pool consistently.
Virginia Beach Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Home prices have stabilized after sharp gains in 2021 and 2022, creating more room to negotiate with motivated sellers.
Days on market have increased slightly, averaging 25 to 35 days — giving investors more time to conduct due diligence.
Short-term rental demand near the Oceanfront remains strong, with average annual revenue for a 2-bedroom unit exceeding $45,000.
New construction is limited by land availability, keeping resale inventory tight in established neighborhoods.
Interest rate pressure has reduced competition from traditional buyers, opening doors for cash investors and creative deal makers.
Investor activity is concentrated in zip codes 23451, 23462, 23464, and 23452 — all worth monitoring for new listings.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Virginia Beach

The best real estate deals in Virginia Beach VA rarely appear on the MLS. They come from motivated sellers who haven't listed yet — people dealing with inherited properties, divorce, financial hardship, or simply tired landlords ready to exit. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is a critical skill in a tight-inventory market like this one. Effective methods include direct mail to absentee owners, driving for dollars in targeted zip codes, probate list marketing, and building relationships with local wholesalers and real estate attorneys.

Once you find a potential deal, don't move forward without doing proper analysis. You can also explore our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to sharpen your evaluation skills before you commit capital.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Virginia Beach

Virginia Beach attracts out-of-state investors because of its economic stability and military tenant base. But remote investing carries real risks without the right local infrastructure in place. Here's what experienced remote investors do to protect themselves in this market.

items: Build a local team first: Find a property manager, a contractor, and a real estate attorney before you close your first deal.
Focus on B-class neighborhoods: Areas like Kempsville and Landstown offer stable tenants and manageable property conditions — less risk than distressed C-class areas.
Use virtual tours and third-party inspections: Never waive inspection contingencies on remote purchases. Hire an independent inspector even on wholesale assignments.
Understand Virginia landlord-tenant law: Virginia has specific rules around security deposits, notice periods, and eviction procedures. Get familiar with them before you place a tenant.
Partner with a local wholesaler or agent: Someone on the ground can alert you to off-market deals and neighborhood shifts you won't see from a distance.
Visit the market at least once: A single trip to walk neighborhoods, meet your team, and see properties in person builds confidence and catches issues no photo can reveal.

sections.content: The investors who succeed remotely aren't lucky — they're systematic. They build local teams, use reliable data, and never let excitement override their numbers.

Pro Tip: Virginia Beach's Flood Zone designations matter enormously for insurance costs and resale value. Always check FEMA flood maps before acquiring any property near the coast or tidal waterways. A property in an AE flood zone can carry insurance premiums 3 to 5 times higher than a comparable home in an X zone.
Is Virginia Beach Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Virginia Beach offers a rare combination of military stability, tourism income potential, and appreciating home values — all in a city large enough to support active deal flow. Whether you're wholesaling for quick assignment fees, flipping for profit, or building a rental portfolio with military tenants, there are legitimate paths to success here. The key is knowing your numbers, working the right neighborhoods, and sourcing deals before they hit the open market.
